design_detail: Registry homepage (MGH National Pregnancy Registry for Psychiatric Medications); citation/URL only
comparison_group: None
population: Pregnancy exposure registry for psychiatric medications (no study population reported in file)
sample_size_detail: Not applicable; website citation only, no data in file
rationale: File contains only the ACOG citation to a registry webpage; no abstract or data. The protocol places registry homepages under 'Not a study (resource)'.

design_detail: AHRQ Comparative Effectiveness Review No. 236: systematic review of perinatal pharmacologic interventions; 4 databases searched to June 2020, surveillance to March 2021; dual screening
comparison_group: Placebo, no treatment, other pharmacotherapy, or discontinuation before pregnancy (per included studies)
population: Pregnant, postpartum, or reproductive-age women with a mental health disorder treated with pharmacotherapy
sample_size_detail: 164 studies (168 articles); total pooled participants not reported in abstract
rationale: AHRQ systematic review of 164 studies including RCTs (e.g., brexanolone vs placebo) and observational harms studies; abstract notes 'More than 95 percent of studies reporting on harms were observational'.

design_detail: Population-based register cohort using linked population health data and birth records, 1998–2001; SSRI exposure in last 14 days of gestation vs exposure stopped earlier; propensity score matching
severity_measure: PS matching on total exposure and 'maternal health characteristics'; abstract states findings hold controlling for maternal illness severity (specific measures not listed)
comparison_group: Neonates with gestational SSRI exposure that stopped before the last 14 days (NL14)
population: Neonates with prenatal SSRI exposure in linked population health/birth records, 1998–2001
sample_size_detail: N = 119,547 linked neonatal birth records (source population); numbers of L14 and NL14 SSRI-exposed neonates in the matched analysis not reported in abstract
rationale: Non-randomized comparison of late vs earlier-stopped SSRI exposure with PS matching; conclusion says results are 'Controlling for maternal illness severity', but covariates are not itemized and the analytic N is not given.

design_detail: Retrospective hospital cohort of antidepressant-exposed infants (maternity ward of a general hospital, 2007–2012); risk-factor analysis for poor neonatal adaptation using odds ratios
severity_measure: Maternal anxiety and depression analysed as risk factors, but unclear whether as diagnoses or severity scores and whether ORs are multivariable
comparison_group: Within exposed infants only: SSRI vs SNRI exposure; formula vs breast/mixed feeding; dose levels (no unexposed group)
population: Infants exposed to antidepressants in the last trimester, admitted to a general-hospital maternity ward, 2007–2012
sample_size_detail: 247 infants; 157 (64%) developed PNA
rationale: Cohort restricted to exposed infants comparing risk factors for PNA. Abstract reports ORs without stating multivariable adjustment or a covariate list, so adjustment and severity cannot be determined.

design_detail: NICE clinical guideline CG192 on antenatal and postnatal mental health (NCBI Bookshelf version, 2018 update)
comparison_group: None
population: Women planning pregnancy, pregnant, or within 1 year postpartum with or at risk of mental health problems
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (guideline)
rationale: NICE clinical guideline covering recognition, assessment and treatment of perinatal mental health problems; PubMed type includes Practice Guideline.

design_detail: Registered Nurses' Association of Ontario best practice guideline on assessment and interventions for perinatal depression; citation/URL only
comparison_group: None
population: People with or at risk of perinatal depression (guideline scope; no study population)
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (guideline)
rationale: Citation identifies the item as a 'Best practice guideline' from a professional nursing body; no abstract or data in file.

design_detail: Cross-sectional 36-question mail survey of obstetrician-gynecologists on depression screening attitudes and practices; predictors of screening practice
comparison_group: None (predictors of screening practice among respondents)
population: Obstetrician-gynecologists responding to a mail survey
sample_size_detail: 282 completed surveys; number mailed and response rate not reported in abstract
rationale: Clinician mail survey describing attitudes and practices; the predictor analysis describes survey responses rather than estimating a treatment effect.

design_detail: Postpartum Support International frontline provider training webpage; citation/URL only
comparison_group: None
population: Training program for providers caring for perinatal patients (no study population)
sample_size_detail: Not applicable; website citation only
rationale: Citation is to a training-program webpage; protocol lists training programs under 'Not a study (resource)'. Perinatal flag reflects the program's perinatal focus; no participants studied.

design_detail: Systematic review and multiple-treatments (network) meta-analysis of RCTs comparing 12 new-generation antidepressants for acute unipolar major depression, 1991–Nov 2007; ITT
comparison_group: Other antidepressants (direct and indirect head-to-head comparisons)
population: Adults with unipolar major depression
sample_size_detail: 117 RCTs with 25,928 participants
rationale: Abstract states 'We systematically reviewed 117 randomised controlled trials (25 928 participants)' and used a multiple-treatments meta-analysis; general adult population.

design_detail: Population-based descriptive case series of pregnancy-associated deaths from suicide or overdose, Colorado 2004–2012; record abstraction; mortality ratios per 100,000 live births
severity_measure: Not applicable (purely descriptive; no exposure comparison or adjustment)
comparison_group: None (contextual demographics of all Colorado women with live births)
population: Women with pregnancy-associated deaths from self-harm (suicide or overdose) in Colorado, 2004–2012
sample_size_detail: 63 self-harm deaths among 211 maternal deaths; detailed records abstracted for 59 (31 overdose, 28 suicide); context group 614,154 women with live births
rationale: Authors describe a case series with 'Descriptive analyses' and population death ratios; no comparative estimate. Coded as descriptive observational (precedes case series in decision order); cases are outcome-defined, not exposed cases.

design_detail: Prospective clinical cohort, Perinatal Psychiatry Service, Hospital Clinic Barcelona, 2005–2008; factors associated with SSRI discontinuation (OR) and rates of reintroduction
severity_measure: EPDS and STAI collected, but abstract does not state any multivariable adjustment or covariates for the OR
comparison_group: Women who maintained SSRI treatment vs women who discontinued on pregnancy confirmation
population: Consecutive pregnant women with DSM-IV depressive or anxiety disorder taking SSRIs at conception, Barcelona perinatal psychiatry service
sample_size_detail: 132 women; 70 (53%) discontinued and 62 maintained; 40 of 70 discontinuers reintroduced treatment
rationale: Prospective cohort comparing SSRI discontinuers with maintainers; group differences and an OR for unplanned pregnancy are reported without stated adjustment, so adjustment status cannot be determined.

design_detail: Prospective naturalistic cohort at 3 specialty centers with monthly psychiatric assessments (SCID); survival analysis of time to MDD relapse by antidepressant maintenance vs discontinuation
severity_measure: Abstract reports HR 5.0 without stating covariates; eligibility required MDD history and euthymia for 3 months before LMP
comparison_group: Women who maintained antidepressant medication throughout pregnancy
population: Pregnant women (<16 weeks) with prior major depression, euthymic on current/recent antidepressants, enrolled at 3 centers, 1999–2003
sample_size_detail: 201 enrolled; headline comparison 82 maintained vs 65 discontinued; 13 miscarried, 5 terminated, 12 lost to follow-up, 8 withdrew
rationale: Non-randomized prospective comparison of maintainers vs discontinuers; abstract gives a hazard ratio but no mention of adjustment or covariates, so adjustment and severity control cannot be determined.

design_detail: Utilization and quality assessment of MCPAP for Moms: encounter data June 2014–Dec 2017 plus provider focus groups and patient in-depth interviews (grounded theory)
severity_measure: Not applicable (program evaluation; no comparative effect estimate)
comparison_group: None
population: Pregnant and postpartum women served by a Massachusetts statewide perinatal psychiatry access program, plus enrolled obstetric providers/staff
sample_size_detail: 3,699 women served; 145 practices enrolled and 1,174 providers trained; 7,444 encounters; 3 focus groups (36 providers/staff) and 10 patient interviews
rationale: Describes program utilization counts and qualitative themes without any comparison group or effect estimate; fits program evaluation/qualitative.

design_detail: Systematic review with meta-analyses and mixed-treatment comparisons of second-generation antidepressants for MDD; literature 1980–Aug 2011
comparison_group: Other second-generation antidepressants (head-to-head)
population: Adults with major depressive disorder
sample_size_detail: 234 studies; pooled participants not reported in abstract
rationale: Included 'randomized trials ... to evaluate efficacy and observational studies with at least 1000 participants to assess harm', so component designs are mixed.

design_detail: FDA drug safety communication (regulatory notice) on SSRI use in pregnancy and persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn; citation/URL only
comparison_group: None
population: Pregnant women using SSRIs and their newborns (notice scope; no study population)
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (regulatory notice)
rationale: Citation is an 'FDA drug safety communication'; protocol lists regulatory notices under 'Not a study (resource)'.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort nested in Medicaid Analytic eXtract (46 states + DC), 2000–2010; restricted to women with depression diagnosis; propensity score stratification and high-dimensional PS; logistic regression
severity_measure: Proxies for depression severity (number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses); also other psychotropic medications and health care use in PS
comparison_group: Women with a depression diagnosis and no antidepressant use during pregnancy
population: Pregnant women enrolled in US Medicaid with live-born infants, 2000–2010
sample_size_detail: Depression-restricted cohort for primary adjusted analysis: 65,316 SSRI, 16,283 non-SSRI, 657,515 unexposed; full source cohort 3,789,330 pregnancies (102,179 SSRI, 26,771 non-SSRI)
rationale: PS model includes 'proxies for depression severity (number of outpatient and inpatient depression diagnoses)'; main adjusted ORs come from the depression-restricted cohort with PS/hdPS stratification.

design_detail: Two-site, three-arm randomized placebo-controlled trial (IPT vs sertraline plus clinical management vs pill placebo plus clinical management), 12 weeks; linear mixed effects regression
comparison_group: Pill placebo plus clinical management (and IPT arm)
population: Breastfeeding and non-breastfeeding women with a major depressive episode in the first postpartum year, Iowa and Rhode Island
sample_size_detail: 162 randomized across 3 arms; number analyzed not reported in abstract; notable non-engagement with assigned condition
rationale: Women 'were randomly assigned to IPT, sertraline-clinical management (CM), or pill placebo-CM'; PubMed type Randomized Controlled Trial.

design_detail: Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of brexanolone infusion vs placebo for postpartum depression
comparison_group: Placebo
population: Women with postpartum depression
sample_size_detail: 3 RCTs reported in 2 articles, 4 active arms; 156 brexanolone, 111 placebo
rationale: Methods state 'Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were included'; pooled n = 267 across 3 RCTs.

design_detail: FDA approved REMS page for Zulresso (brexanolone); citation/URL only
comparison_group: None
population: Patients receiving brexanolone for postpartum depression (REMS scope; no study population)
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (regulatory resource)
rationale: Citation is to an FDA REMS webpage, a regulatory resource with no study data.

design_detail: Meta-analysis of RCTs of psychotherapies and medications vs control conditions for GAD; databases searched to June 2017; random effects, Hedges' g, meta-regression
comparison_group: Pill placebo, waitlist, psychological placebo, or treatment as usual
population: Adults with DSM-diagnosed generalized anxiety disorder (child studies excluded)
sample_size_detail: 79 RCTs with 11,002 participants
rationale: Full text: '79 studies with 11,002 participants met the final inclusion criteria'; non-RCTs were excluded.

design_detail: Clinical review of diagnosis and management of perinatal anxiety in the obstetric setting, informed by authors' practice
comparison_group: None
population: Women with perinatal anxiety disorders
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (narrative review)
rationale: Abstract describes a 'concise summary of current research' informed by the authors' clinical practice; no systematic methods described.

design_detail: Meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials of SSRIs, SNRIs, and benzodiazepines for adult GAD (HAM-A outcome); random effects, meta-regression
comparison_group: Pill placebo
population: Adults with a primary diagnosis of generalized anxiety disorder
sample_size_detail: 54 articles reporting 56 trials; 6,464 on active medication, 6,191 on placebo
rationale: Inclusion required 'a randomized, placebo-controlled trial'; 56 unique trials with 12,655 participants pooled.

design_detail: Meta-analysis of cohort and case-control studies of first-trimester benzodiazepine exposure and major malformations or oral cleft; random effects; duplicate extraction
comparison_group: Concurrent unexposed controls (per included studies)
population: Pregnancies with first-trimester benzodiazepine exposure
sample_size_detail: 23 included studies (74 retrieved from >1400 reviewed); pooled participants not reported in abstract
rationale: Meta-analysis of 'cohort and case-control studies'; 23 studies included, analysed separately by design.

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of longitudinal studies of recurrence after first-onset postpartum psychosis (PRISMA/MOOSE; STROBE quality)
comparison_group: None (pooled proportion with isolated postpartum psychosis)
population: Women with first-onset postpartum psychosis within 1 year after childbirth, follow-up of 18 months or more
sample_size_detail: 6 studies, 645 patients; follow-up 11–26 years
rationale: Systematic review/meta-analysis of 6 longitudinal (observational, STROBE-rated) studies pooling 645 patients.

design_detail: Population-based record-linkage cohort (psychiatric case register + prospectively recorded obstetric data), Western Australia 1980–1992; odds ratios vs randomly selected comparison births
severity_measure: Exposure is the maternal diagnosis itself; abstract does not describe any adjustment or covariates for ORs
comparison_group: Randomly selected births to women without a psychiatric diagnosis
population: Women with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or major depression giving birth in Western Australia, 1980–1992
sample_size_detail: 3,174 births to women with schizophrenia or major affective disorders; 3,129 comparison births
rationale: Non-randomized comparison of births to women with severe mental illness vs controls; 'Odds ratios were calculated' with no adjustment described. Also compares pregnancies before vs after diagnosis, unclear if within-mother.

design_detail: Prospective observational PK study (Emory epilepsy and women's mental health programs); population nonlinear mixed-effects (NONMEM) model of lamotrigine oral clearance across pregnancy and postpartum
comparison_group: None (within-woman change from preconception baseline clearance)
population: Women aged 17+ treated with lamotrigine for epilepsy and/or psychiatric disorder (mostly bipolar) who were pregnant or planning pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 60 women, 64 pregnancies, 600 lamotrigine concentrations (43 epilepsy, 19 psychiatric, 2 both pregnancies)
rationale: Models lamotrigine clearance changes with gestational age and postpartum weeks; no clinical outcome comparison.

design_detail: Population-based descriptive cohort of prevalence and trends of antipsychotic use in pregnancy, 11 US health plans (MEPREP) linked to birth certificates, 2001–2007
severity_measure: Not applicable (descriptive prevalence; no adjusted comparison)
comparison_group: None (descriptive comparison of maternal characteristics with unexposed deliveries)
population: Live-born deliveries to women aged 15–45 continuously enrolled in 11 US health plans, 2001–2007
sample_size_detail: 585,615 deliveries; 4,223 atypical-antipsychotic-exposed and 548 typical-antipsychotic-exposed
rationale: Estimates prevalence by year, trimester and diagnosis; no outcome comparison or confounder adjustment.

design_detail: Prospective pregnancy registry cohort (MGH National Pregnancy Registry for Atypical Antipsychotics) with medical-record confirmation; crude odds ratio for major malformations
severity_measure: Abstract never states whether the OR is adjusted (Amendment 1 rule b); comparison group restricted to women with psychiatric histories (diagnosis only)
comparison_group: Unexposed infants of women with histories of psychiatric morbidity
population: Pregnant women aged 18–45 enrolled in a US registry based at Massachusetts General Hospital, through December 2014
sample_size_detail: 487 enrolled (353 SGA users, 134 comparison); 303 completed and eligible: 214 first-trimester-exposed live births vs 89 controls
rationale: Registry cohort comparing SGA-exposed vs unexposed psychiatric controls; adjustment of the OR is never stated (Amendment 1b). OR 1.25 equals a crude calculation from 3/214 vs 1/89.

design_detail: Prospective observational cohort (Pittsburgh, 2006–2011); repeated-measures mixed models of Bayley scores: Model I unadjusted, Model II adds SIGH-ADS and MRS, Model III adds selected confounders
severity_measure: Maternal symptom-severity scores: SIGH-ADS (Hamilton depression) and Mania Rating Scale
comparison_group: Infants of women with untreated bipolar disorder (BD−) and of controls without bipolar disorder or psychotropic exposure
population: Mother-infant dyads of pregnant women with bipolar disorder treated (BD+) or untreated (BD−) with psychotropics and controls, Pittsburgh, 2006–2011
sample_size_detail: 54 BD+, 27 BD−, 116 controls; 52-week retention 52–83% by group
rationale: Models II–III adjust for SIGH-ADS and MRS symptom scores. The abstract's headline motor-quality result comes from unadjusted Model I and became nonsignificant (P=.0529) after symptom adjustment.

design_detail: Descriptive surveillance analysis of spina bifida incidence from 16 state population-based birth defects surveillance systems, 1983–1990 (MMWR)
comparison_group: None
population: Births in 16 US states with population-based birth defects surveillance, 1983–1990
sample_size_detail: Number of births or cases not given (abstract truncated)
rationale: CDC analysis 'to determine the incidence and descriptive epidemiology of spina bifida' from surveillance reports; purely descriptive.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, 4 Dutch provinces, births 1972–1992; antiepileptic-drug-regimen-specific relative risks of major congenital abnormalities vs matched nonepileptic controls
severity_measure: Matching factors and covariates not described in abstract; no mention of epilepsy severity or seizure type
comparison_group: Nonepileptic matched controls (and comparisons between AED regimens)
population: Children born 1972–1992 in 4 Netherlands provinces to mothers with epilepsy using AEDs in the first trimester
sample_size_detail: 1,411 AED-exposed children; 2,000 nonepileptic matched controls
rationale: Non-randomized comparison using 'nonepileptic matched controls', so some matching-based adjustment; matching variables and any severity measures cannot be determined from the abstract.

design_detail: Prospective hospital cohort of pregnancies in women with epilepsy, San Paolo Hospital, Milan, since 1977; monthly AED levels; descriptive malformation rates
severity_measure: Only crude malformation rates reported (including the untreated subgroup); no adjustment described
comparison_group: 25 untreated women with epilepsy (crude)
population: Pregnancies of women with epilepsy followed by epileptologists and obstetricians at San Paolo Hospital, Milan, from 1977
sample_size_detail: 517 pregnancies followed; 25 untreated patients
rationale: Reports overall malformation rate (9.7%) and none among 25 untreated patients; no adjusted analysis described despite stated aim to detect risk factors.

design_detail: Non-systematic review of animal and human data on anticonvulsant teratogenicity with clinical recommendations
comparison_group: None
population: Experimental animals and women exposed to anticonvulsants in pregnancy (and their infants)
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (narrative review)
rationale: Abstract summarizes animal research and human data and gives prescribing advice, with no methods or new data; reads as a narrative review.

design_detail: Case-control study within the Spanish Collaborative Study of Congenital Malformations (ECEMC); first-trimester valproic acid exposure and limb deficiencies; OR adjusted for potential confounders
severity_measure: OR reported after controlling for potential confounders, but covariates not listed; no epilepsy severity mentioned
comparison_group: Non-malformed control infants
population: Consecutive malformed infants (excluding genetic syndromes) and control newborns in the Spanish ECEMC registry with antiepileptic drug data
sample_size_detail: 22,294 malformed infants and 21,937 controls; 57 malformed and 10 control infants VPA-exposed; 3 limb deficiencies among VPA-exposed; number of limb-deficiency cases in the analysis not given
rationale: Case-control analysis yielding OR 6.17 'after controlling for potential confounder factors'; adjustment exists but covariate list is unavailable.

design_detail: Letter (J Pediatr 1983) with no abstract; presumed report of valproate-exposed case(s), inferred from title only
comparison_group: Unclear (no abstract)
population: Infants with prenatal valproate exposure (inferred from title)
sample_size_detail: No abstract; number of cases not reported in file
rationale: File has only metadata: PubMed type 'Letter' and title 'Possible teratogenic effect of valproate during pregnancy'. Coded as case report by inference; design cannot be verified.

design_detail: Case report of two VPA-exposed siblings with long-term follow-up plus literature review compiling 69 published VPA-monotherapy cases (1978–2000)
comparison_group: None
population: Children with prenatal valproic acid monotherapy exposure (fetal valproate syndrome)
sample_size_detail: 2 new sibling cases described; 69 published cases compiled in the literature review (unclear whether the siblings are included)
rationale: Describes exposed cases without a comparison group; phenotype frequencies come from the 69 reviewed cases. The 'siblings' are case subjects, not a sibling-comparison design.

design_detail: Clinical case series of children with fetal anticonvulsant syndromes (standardized questionnaire, interview, examination)
comparison_group: None
population: Children with fetal anticonvulsant syndromes ascertained via a support association (52) and Aberdeen Medical Genetics Service referrals (5)
sample_size_detail: 57 children: 34 valproate alone, 4 carbamazepine alone, 4 phenytoin alone, 15 polytherapy
rationale: Describes 57 exposed, affected children with no comparison group.

design_detail: Unselected case series of valproate-exposed infants of epileptic mothers; within-series association of findings with maternal valproate dose
comparison_group: None (within-series dose comparisons only)
population: Infants born to epileptic mothers and exposed to sodium valproate during pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 17 infants; 9 with minor abnormalities (5 also major malformations), 9 with withdrawal manifestations
rationale: 'An unselected series' of 17 exposed infants without an unexposed comparison group.

design_detail: AIUM practice parameter for the performance of fetal echocardiography (no abstract in file)
comparison_group: None
population: Pregnancies undergoing fetal echocardiography
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (practice parameter)
rationale: Title identifies a professional 'Practice Parameter'; PubMed type Practice Guideline. File has metadata only, no abstract.

design_detail: Prospective measurement of maternal and umbilical cord lithium concentrations at delivery, pooled with published cases; placental passage ratio and concentration-outcome associations
severity_measure: Not applicable (PK study; concentration-outcome associations not described as confounder-adjusted)
comparison_group: None (infants with higher vs lower lithium concentrations at delivery)
population: Pregnant women treated with lithium through delivery and their infants
sample_size_detail: 10 prospectively studied participants plus 32 cases from MEDLINE/PsycINFO searches, analysed as pooled data
rationale: Primary aim is quantifying placental passage (cord-to-maternal ratio 1.05) and effects of withholding lithium; outcome associations by concentration are not confounder-adjusted per abstract.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, US Medicaid Analytic eXtract 2000–2007, restricted to women with mood/anxiety disorder diagnoses; GEE relative risks with covariate adjustment plus hdPS sensitivity analysis
severity_measure: Proxies of mood/anxiety disorder severity: number of outpatient and inpatient mood/anxiety diagnoses; also other psychotropics and health care use
comparison_group: Women with mood/anxiety disorder diagnoses and no antidepressant supply in the 5 months before delivery
population: Pregnant women aged 12–55 with mood or anxiety disorder diagnoses in US Medicaid, live births 2000–2007
sample_size_detail: Subcohort of 106,000 with mood/anxiety disorders minus 3,278 polytherapy users: 69,044 unexposed, 29,222 SRI monotherapy (12,710 current), 4,456 non-SRI (1,495 current); eligible population 2,759,414 pregnancies
rationale: Fully adjusted models include 'proxies of mood/anxiety disorder severity' (counts of outpatient and inpatient diagnoses) within a cohort restricted to mood/anxiety disorders.

design_detail: Prospective national register-based birth cohort, Finland 1996–2010; hazard ratios for speech/language, scholastic and motor disorders through age 14
severity_measure: Comparison restricted to mothers with depression-related diagnoses (diagnosis only); any covariate adjustment not described in abstract
comparison_group: Offspring of mothers with depression-related psychiatric disorders without SSRI purchases (unmedicated); also offspring of unexposed mothers without psychiatric diagnosis
population: Singleton offspring in Finnish national registers, born 1996–2010
sample_size_detail: 15,596 SSRI-exposed, 9,537 unmedicated, 31,207 unexposed; sampling frame of 845,345 pregnant women
rationale: Non-randomized comparison of SSRI-exposed vs unmedicated depressed mothers' offspring; abstract gives HR 1.37 but does not say whether or for what it is adjusted, so adjustment and severity cannot be determined.
